item.title: McCutcheon breaks national record twice
item.description: FIJI swimmer Anahira McCutcheon delivered one of team Fiji’s standout performances at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, breaking the Fiji open women’s 50-metre butterfly record twice in the space of a day. McCutcheon first set a new national mark of 27.09 seconds in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI swimmer Anahira McCutcheon delivered one of team Fiji’s standout performances at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, breaking the Fiji open women’s 50-metre butterfly record twice in the space of a day.

McCutcheon first set a new national mark of 27.09 seconds in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals.

She then went a few milliseconds quicker in the semi-finals clocking a time of 27.01 seconds to lower her record and complete a memorable day in the pool.

The double record-breaking effort was a major milestone for the young swimmer and one of Fiji’s highlights at the games.

In the men’s event, Samuel Yalimaiwai and Don younger competed in the 100m breaststroke, recording times of 1 minute 5.60 seconds and 1: 08.18 respectively.

Fiji’s men’s 4x100m freestyle relay team of Reuben Taylor, Don Younger, Hansel McCaig and Tolu Baledrokadroka also impressed, finishing in 3:33.08.

Taylor produced an outstanding opening leg, posting a personal best of 53.38 seconds to give Fiji a strong start.

The performances continue team Fiji’s impressive campaign in the pool, with national records and personal bests highlighting the progress of the country’s swimmers.

item.title: Wheelbarrow race raises record $250k
item.description: THE Frank Hilton Amazing Wheelbarrow Race has raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities across Fiji, marking the most successful fundraising campaign in the event’s 10-year history. The amount eclipsed last year’s total of $166,000, reflecting the growing support from businesses, sponsors and the wider community for the fundraiser, which continues to change the lives of childr
item.content:encoded:
THE Frank Hilton Amazing Wheelbarrow Race has raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities across Fiji, marking the most successful fundraising campaign in the event’s 10-year history.

The amount eclipsed last year’s total of $166,000, reflecting the growing support from businesses, sponsors and the wider community for the fundraiser, which continues to change the lives of children and their families through the services provided by Frank Hilton Organisation (FHO).

A total of 25 teams lined up for this year’s race, with Fortech emerging as the overall champion after a spirited day of competition.

However, organisers said the event has always been about much more than crossing the finish line first.

Celebrating a decade since the race was first introduced, organisers highlighted the impact the fundraiser has had over the past 10 years, describing the milestone as a celebration of lives transformed through the generosity of participants and supporters.

“This represents lives supported, services delivered and futures changed,” organisers said during the prize-giving ceremony.

They acknowledged that every team, sponsor and individual who participated had contributed to improving the lives of children with disabilities by helping them access vital support services provided by FHO.

“In your wheelbarrow you have carried hope, dignity and opportunity for the children and families we serve,” organisers told participants.

The event has evolved into one of FHO’s flagship fundraising activities, bringing together corporate organisations and community groups in a unique competition while raising awareness about the needs of children living with disabilities across Fiji.

Although Fortech claimed top honours in the race itself, Harcourts was recognised as the highest fundraising team after collecting the largest amount in donations, with Begel Boys finishing second in the fundraising category.

A total of six awards were presented during the prize-giving ceremony to recognise achievements in both racing and fundraising.

Organisers thanked all 25 participating teams, sponsors, volunteers and supporters for helping make the 10th anniversary event the most successful in the history of the Wheelbarrow Race.

They said the record fundraising total would enable FHO to continue delivering essential services and support programmes to children with disabilities and their families across Fiji, ensuring more children have access to opportunities that improve their quality of life and future.

item.title: Setareki leads Grammar back to Southern Zone glory
item.description: Suva Grammar School under-19 captain Setareki Radrodrolagi’s belief never wavered, even after his side suffered its only defeat of the Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby competition to Nasinu Secondary School in round six. That confidence was rewarded yesterday as Radrodrolagi led Grammar to a thrilling 25-19 victory over Nasinu in the U19 final, completing a remarkable turnaround and reclaimin
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School under-19 captain Setareki Radrodrolagi’s belief never wavered, even after his side suffered its only defeat of the Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby competition to Nasinu Secondary School in round six.

That confidence was rewarded yesterday as Radrodrolagi led Grammar to a thrilling 25-19 victory over Nasinu in the U19 final, completing a remarkable turnaround and reclaiming the Southern Zone title.

The right deadlocks, who hails from Navucini in Naitasiri and has maternal links to Nakasaleka, Lagalevu in Kadavu, said the round-six loss became the motivation the team needed heading into the knockout stages.

“We lost to Nasinu in round six, but I told the boys to regroup because we would meet them again in the final,” Radrodrolagi said.

“We just had to reset, stay focused and believe in ourselves.”

His prediction came true as Grammar produced a determined performance to deny Nasinu the title in one of the most anticipated finals of the day.

Radrodrolagi said the team’s focus now shifts to the Vodafone Deans competition, where they hope to continue their winning momentum.

“We’re not going there just to participate. We’re going there to compete,” he said.

The captain admitted the victory was especially meaningful because Suva Grammar had not enjoyed the same level of dominance in the U19 grade over the past few years.

“This means a lot to us. Grammar has always had a proud rugby tradition and we’re happy to bring the Southern Zone title back to the school,” he said.

He also praised his teammates for their resilience throughout the campaign, saying every player contributed to the team’s success after bouncing back from the disappointment of their earlier defeat.

Radrodrolagi dedicated the championship to former teammate Paolo Bonolangi, who is currently in France, and to his coach for their guidance, encouragement and unwavering belief in the squad throughout the season.

The remaining finals also produced exciting contests across the grades. The U14 final between Suva Grammar 20-10 againts Marist Brothers High School, while Grammar claimed the U15 title with a 24-17 win over Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School.

MGM defeated Nasinu Secondary School 19-12 to win the U16 boys’ title, and Grammar edged Gospel High School 23-22 in the U17 final. In the Weet-Bix Raluve competition, Nasinu defeated Suva Grammar 15-12, while Lomary Secondary School defeated Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School 18-0 to secure the U18 title.

item.title: Super subs help RKS
item.description: The Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS) under-16 teams bench proved the difference as the Lodoni boys pulled away in the second half to defeat Queen Victoria School (QVS) 23-8 and claim the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union under-16 title at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva yesterday. item.content:encoded:
The Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS) under-16 teams bench proved the difference as the Lodoni boys pulled away in the second half to defeat Queen Victoria School (QVS) 23-8 and claim the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union under-16 title at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva yesterday.

Leading 13-8 at the break, RKS faced a determined QVS outfit before their replacements injected fresh energy into the contest.

The impact of the substitutes mirrored a “bomb squad”, lifting the tempo and helping RKS cross for two unanswered tries in the final quarter to seal a convincing victory.

Head coach Phillip Halofaki said the halftime message centred on unity and faith.

“To work hard as a team, as brothers, through the Holy Spirit we could overcome anything,” he said.

While pleased with the performance, Halofaki believes his side still has plenty of improvement ahead of the national quarter-finals.

Despite winning the Eastern Zone crown, he said RKS would embrace the underdog tag against the country’s top schools.

“We respect Suva Grammar School and Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School.

“We still have a lot to work on, and we give glory to the Almighty for today’s victory,” he said.

Meanwhile, QVS claimed the U14 title after edging RKS 13-7.

Lelean Memorial School upset RKS 12-7 to win the Under-15 final, while RKS bounced back in the U17 grade with a 24-15 victory over QVS.

Lelean completed a memorable day by defeating RKS 23-17 in the U19 final.

In the Raluve U16 final, Adi Cakobau School held off Saint Vincent College 19-18 in a thrilling contest.

Results: U14: QVS 13-7 RKS, U15: LMS 12-7 RKS, U16: RKS 23-8 QVS, U17: RKS 24-13, U18…..U19: RKS 17-23 LMS. Raluve: U16 ACS 19-18 St Vincent.

item.title: Waratahs retain Super W title
item.description: THE NSW Waratahs successfully defended their Super W title after defeating the McDonald’s Fijian Drua Women 34-17 at 4R Stadium in Ba yesterday. The Waratahs controlled the opening half with strong possession, disciplined defence and clinical execution. Winger Maya Stewart crossed for the opening try before vice-captain Desiree Miller added the conversion for a 7-0 lead.
item.content:encoded:
THE NSW Waratahs successfully defended their Super W title after defeating the McDonald’s Fijian Drua Women 34-17 at 4R Stadium in Ba yesterday.

The Waratahs controlled the opening half with strong possession, disciplined defence and clinical execution. Winger Maya Stewart crossed for the opening try before vice-captain Desiree Miller added the conversion for a 7-0 lead.

The visitors continued to dominate territory and possession, with Miller scoring their second try. Although she was unable to convert, the Waratahs took a deserved 12-0 advantage into halftime.

The Waratahs started the second half strongly, extending their lead when prop Faliki Pohiva powered over for their third try, with Miller adding the extras.

They continued to apply pressure and secured their fourth try through Rosie Ferguson, although the conversion attempt was unsuccessful.

The Drua responded through Naitasiri native Nunia Daunimoala, who crossed for the hosts’ first try, but the conversion was missed.

The Waratahs answered with another try through Amelia Whitaker before she grabbed her second of the match in the 67th minute after backing herself to dive over in the corner.

The Drua refused to give up, with winger Atelaite Buna slicing through the Waratahs defence to create the opportunity for Daunimoala to score her second try. Varanisese Qoro was unable to add the conversion.

The home side finished strongly when Sulita Waisega crossed for their third try, with Qoro converting. Despite the late Drua fightback, the Waratahs remained in control to seal a 34-17 victory and successfully defend their Super W championship.

item.title: Winning skipper hails team’s belief, composure
item.description: THE NSW Waratahs victory against the McDonald’s Fijian Fiji Drua Women side marks another successful chapter for the Australian Women side in front of a passionate Fijian crowd in the Super Rugby W Grand Final at Four R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba yesterday. Team captain Emily Chancellor says belief and composure were the driving forces behind her side’s 34-17 victory over the McDonald’s Fiji Fijia
item.content:encoded:
THE NSW Waratahs victory against the McDonald’s Fijian Fiji Drua Women side marks another successful chapter for the Australian Women side in front of a passionate Fijian crowd in the Super Rugby W Grand Final at Four R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba yesterday.

Team captain Emily Chancellor says belief and composure were the driving forces behind her side’s 34-17 victory over the McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women.

The defending champions weathered an early onslaught from the Drua before taking control to successfully retain the title.

Chancellor said the opening exchanges were crucial, with her side forced to absorb relentless pressure from the home team.

“The crowd was amazing. The Drua came at us in that first 10 minutes and we had to defend so hard to keep them out. That really set the tone for how we wanted to play,” she said.

She credited her team’s faith in its game plan, saying the Waratahs remained patient and trusted their processes despite the physical challenge posed by the Drua.

“We know how good we are when we’ve got the ball in attacking zones.

“They had a really strong defensive game and when they ran directly at us, we struggled at times, but I’m so proud of my team for the way they controlled themselves.”

The experienced skipper revealed the Waratahs had placed a strong emphasis on mindset leading into the final.

“We trained and talked about mindset and the desire to have belief. We truly believed we could do it today.”

Although delighted with the result, Chancellor believes there is still room for improvement.

“We’ve always talked about wanting that 80-minute performance and I still don’t think we gave as good as we can.

“But we were more consistent and every time they scored, we responded.”

She also praised the leadership within the squad, saying calm decision-makers helped steer the team through key moments.

“It makes it easy when you know the simple process you’re supposed to do. Then it’s just your job to execute.”

The NSW Waratahs will face the winner of the Super Rugby Women Aupiki final.

item.title: Young Bula Boys fall short against New Zealand
item.description: Fiji’s dream of lifting the OFC Under-16 Men’s Championship ended in disappointment after a dominant New Zealand side claimed a 12th tournament title with a convincing 5-0 victory in the final at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby. The Junior Bula Boys were outplayed by the defending champions, who completed another unbeaten campaign after scoring 24 goals in five matches throughout the tour
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s dream of lifting the OFC Under-16 Men’s Championship ended in disappointment after a dominant New Zealand side claimed a 12th tournament title with a convincing 5-0 victory in the final at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

The Junior Bula Boys were outplayed by the defending champions, who completed another unbeaten campaign after scoring 24 goals in five matches throughout the tournament.

New Zealand made the perfect start, taking the lead after just 90 seconds when Zach Cashmore headed home from a corner to score the fastest goal ever recorded in an OFC Under-16 Championship final.

Fiji struggled to contain the attacking pressure and conceded twice more before halftime.

Davi Valles Dos Santos doubled New Zealand’s advantage in the 36th minute after Fiji failed to clear the danger inside the penalty area before an unfortunate own goal by defender Somit Maharaj in first-half stoppage time gave New Zealand a commanding 3-0 lead at the break.

Despite the scoreline, Fiji showed glimpses of promise in the second half.

Ryan Swami came closest for the Junior Bula Boys, sending a powerful effort over the crossbar from a corner as Fiji searched for a way back into the contest.

However, another defensive mistake proved costly.

Substitute Jack Clegg capitalised on a turnover inside the penalty box to score New Zealand’s fourth goal in the 76th minute, only moments after coming off the bench.

Clegg then turned provider four minutes later, intercepting another loose pass before setting up Valles Dos Santos, who scored his second goal of the match to seal a comprehensive 5-0 victory.

The win secured New Zealand’s 11th consecutive OFC Under-16 Men’s Championship title and their 12th overall, underlining their continued dominance in Oceania youth football.

While Fiji fell short in the final, reaching only its third OFC Under-16 Championship final remains a significant achievement for the young side and secures qualification for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup, alongside champions New Zealand.

item.title: NSW Waratahs claim historic seventh title with strong performance over Fijian Drua
item.description: The NSW Waratahs have come home strongly in the Super Rugby Women’s final, a disciplined and focused performance seeing them prevail 34-17 over the Fijian Drua in Ba. The Fijian fans showed again why they are some of the most passionate in world rugby, with a 4,097-strong crowd welcoming both sides to Ba.
item.content:encoded:
The NSW Waratahs have come home strongly in the Super Rugby Women’s final, a disciplined and focused performance seeing them prevail 34-17 over the Fijian Drua in Ba.

The Fijian fans showed again why they are some of the most passionate in world rugby, with a 4,097-strong crowd welcoming both sides to Ba.

However, despite coming into the weekend having done finals the hard way, the Waratahs started well, with Maya Stewart getting the visitors on the board inside the first 20 minutes.

Both sides saw plenty of opportunities to score, but the Drua’s handling errors and issues at the lineout proved a critical point of difference, and in the 28th minute the visitors went further ahead thanks to a strong effort from Desiree Miller.

The Drua pushed hard in the final ten minutes, however some brilliant cover defence by Caitlyn Halse saw the visitors hold on to take a 12-0 lead into the break.

The Drua’s errors continued early in the second half, with a knock on early in the second half on their own try line seeing Faliki Pohiva, who had put on several big hits in a player-of-the-match performance, scoring the Waratahs’ third in the 47th minute.

The backs then continued their form, with Rosie Ferguson cutting the defensive line to pieces five minutes later to score the Waratahs’ fourth – the score jumping out to a 24-0 lead.

The hosts turned to their forwards to make the hard yards, and found some success when Nunia Daunimoala barged over on the hour mark to give the hosts a sniff with 20 minutes to play.

However, a stunning double to substitute Amelia Whittaker in five minutes put the visitors out to a 34-5 lead with ten minutes to play.

Daunimoala would score a second try for the hosts with ten minutes to play, but the Waratahs wound the clock down well, Sulita Waisega managing only one more try after the siren to give the crowd something to cheer about.

Holding back tears, Bitila Tawake earned plenty of love from the home crowd on a special day for the competition.

“It took us five years to get the home grand final, and I’m sorry we didn’t get the win today,” Tawake said.

“The Waratahs, the best of the best. We gave our one hundred, you gave your one hundred, but at the end of the day, you guys won.

“The goal for the club is to get another grand final, and I promise we’ll get that again.”

“We dream at home of playing in front of crowds like you guys,” NSW Waratahs captain Chancellor said in accepting the title.

“You know how to support rugby, to come out and be so loud and so energetic, it lights my heart to know how much support women’s rugby has.

“Everytime we come out and play Fiji, we know we’re gonna have an incredible game. The way you play, with direct rugby, creative offloads, it’s a really tough game to play.

“We had 15 coaches and 40+ players that have contributed to this [season], we have 34 girls that have taken the field this season, and we’ve had six girls that have had injuries that have put them out or made it a really tough season for them.

“I want to shoutout every single player that’s been part of this program this year.

“Rugby in Australia wrote us off, we lose two games and that’s it for us. This is that response and I’m so proud of this team!”
